title: Build a hiring process that keeps its context
description: Connect candidate sourcing, interview preparation, meeting notes, and team handoffs.
introduction: A useful recruiting workflow does more than produce a long candidate list. It preserves why someone fits, what the team learned, and what should happen next across sourcing, interviews, outreach, and the ATS.

Begin with one role, one evidence standard, and one result the team can review. Strawberry can learn through a few questions, relevant connected apps, or both, then preserve the accepted process once it works.

sections.title: Start with the role and the evidence
paragraphs: Clarify what success looks like in the role, the evidence that matters, useful adjacent backgrounds, and the team’s real dealbreakers. Existing scorecards, strong examples, rejection patterns, and ATS context should be inspected before the user is asked to repeat them.

Source across relevant professional evidence such as LinkedIn, GitHub, portfolios, and personal sites. Review a varied first batch before expanding the search, keep real source links, and show how many profiles were reviewed and filtered.

skills.context: Use this to source a reviewable first group of candidates.

sections.title: Carry context through the pipeline
paragraphs: Before proposing ATS changes, cross-reference profiles, portfolios, role changes, duplicates, and existing pipeline state. Preserve why the team advanced or rejected someone rather than reducing the decision to an unexplained score.

Prepare interviewers from the job description, calendar, prior correspondence, ATS notes, portfolio, GitHub, and current public evidence. Afterward, preserve decisions and follow-ups in the team’s accepted destination.

skills.context: Use this to prepare for candidate interviews.
Use this to preserve interview decisions and follow-ups.

sections.title: Reach out in the team’s voice
paragraphs: Learn from approved past messages or brand material, research only enough verified context to make the opportunity relevant, and draft a small sample before scaling. Messages stay as drafts until approved.
LinkedIn work moves sequentially at human speed, keeps real profile URLs, and stops on warnings or uncertainty.

skills.context: Draft and send reviewable candidate outreach in the team’s voice, adding a sequence when useful.

sections.title: Keep the ATS useful without losing judgment
paragraphs: Strawberry can cross-reference candidates against the existing pipeline, flag duplicates, and prepare approved stage, note, or follow-up changes. The important part is preserving the evidence and team reasoning behind a decision rather than replacing it with an unexplained score.
Review the proposed mapping and one real update before expanding it. Consequential changes stay visible and reviewable.

skills.context: Create an evidence-backed first review of incoming applicants.

sections.title: Make the accepted hiring process repeatable
paragraphs: Once a workflow is useful, preserve its criteria, evidence standard, outreach voice, destinations, and approval points as a team-specific skill. Add a Routine only when the underlying process has worked and the team wants it to recur.
Shared hiring work should make handoffs clearer, not hide them. Agree on ownership and verify one real handoff before scaling.

skills.context: Turn a trusted recruiting workflow into a shared team process.
